name: DEQ Pollution Response Program (PReP) public report API (myDEQ portal)
operator: Virginia Department of Environmental Quality, Office of Pollution Response and Emergency Preparedness
waters_covered: statewide; receptor waterbody named per report
access_detail: JSON API behind the public PReP search page (Vue app; found in the page bundle). GET https://portal.deq.virginia.gov/prep/api/prepReports?orderBy=incidentDateTime%20desc&limit=N&offset=M&expand=prepStatusCode ; any record column works as a filter (sewageRelated=Y, incidentDateTimeFrom=YYYY-MM-DD, incidentDateTimeTo, siteFipsCodesId, id). Detail: /prep/api/prepReports/{id}?expand=prepStatusCode,prepFipsCode.fipsRegion,prepReportAgencies,prepReceptorImpactCode,prepReportSewages,prepStatusReasonCode,prepIntentionCode . Sewage sub-record: /prep/api/prepReportSewages?reportId={id}&expand=prepComponentTypeCode,prepSewageCauses.prepCauseCode,prepSewageImpacts.prepImpactTypeCode,prepSewageRemediations.prepRemediationCode . Also prepReportEvents, prepReportMaterials, prepReportReleaseSubtypes. No login, no key. Response wrapper {offset,limit,count,total,results}. total=117,586 on 2026-11-02; 419 reports with incidentDateTime since 2026-10-01, 111 of them sewageRelated=Y. Newest record created the same day (2026-11-02 13:51). Saved raw/prep/*.json. Status log: /prep/api/prepReportEvents?reportId={id}&expand=prepEventTypeCode&orderBy=eventDate%20desc (e.g. 324738: Call Received 2026-08-04T21:30:30, Under Investigation and Assigned 2026-08-05T10:55:36), which can fill revision_history.

sample_record.incidentComment: DEQ received a report stating, Sanitary sewer overflow at manhole that entered the nearest stormwater structure.

prepReportSewages.correctiveAction: Norfolk Storm water notified Norfolk Utilities

fills_event_fields: event_type (sewageRelated + siteName prefix SSO/CSO; incident types only in the export layer)
cannot_fill: ended_at (incidentEndDateTime almost always null; derive from duration hours)
coordinates (none in the API; use the EDMA point layer)
cadence: Live: records appear within minutes of a call-center or online report (records created 2026-11-02 seen the same afternoon). Permittees must call within 24 hours (Va. Code § 62.1-44.5 B; 9VAC25-31-190 L 6-7) and file a written report within 5 days; DEQ staff then update volume, cause and status over days to weeks (Douglas Ave record modified 13 days later).
history: Records from previous systems back to before 2008; current PReP schema since 2019-05-29; fields renamed 2022-09-09 (older rows keep old names).
license: Page text: "If downloaded information will be distributed to other entities, the following statement should be included: 'DEQ is the data source. DEQ does not certify that this data represents a complete record. This data is provided to the citizens of the Commonwealth free of charge and for informational purposes only.'" Terms of Use on the same page: information "SHOULD NOT BE RELIED UPON FOR PERSONAL, MEDICAL, LEGAL OR FINANCIAL DECISIONS"; "By downloading any dataset, you are affirmatively stating that you have read and understood these Terms of Use". https://www.deq.virginia.gov/land-waste/pollution-response/pollution-data-and-reporting
legal_basis: Va. Code § 62.1-44.5 B; 9VAC25-31-190 L 6 and L 7; Va. Code § 62.1-44.19:6 B (DEQ dissemination)
status_reason: The best statewide event feed: live, JSON, filterable by sewage flag and date, with volume, receiving water, cause and NRC/VDEM/SSORS cross-ids. Undocumented internal API, so treat as fragile; the ArcGIS export is the documented fallback.
notes: Data quality: free-text waterbody names ("Gillie Creek", "Gravel Run"), duplicate records for one event (Douglas Ave = 324738 and 324765), permit-number field sometimes holds an MS4 permit (VA0088650 = Norfolk MS4), mediaType sometimes wrong (an SSO coded Petroleum). Routine permitted wet-weather CSOs are not reported here (only 3 CSO-named records since 2024).

name: DEQ PReP Report Export All (ArcGIS table; GeoHub / data.virginia.gov dataset)
access_detail: ArcGIS 12.1 MapServer table (no geometry), maxRecordCount 2000, supports statistics. Query: .../MapServer/0/query?where=SEWAGE_RELATED%3D%27Y%27&outFields=*&orderByFields=INCIDENT_DATE_TIME%20DESC&f=json . Hub item 1b01cc4bd6e54d4e9f8f22195415b2a5 (owner arthur.s.kay_VADEQ, recordCount 117,334); CSV/GeoJSON/KML downloads at https://geohub-vadeq.hub.arcgis.com/api/download/v1/items/1b01cc4bd6e54d4e9f8f22195415b2a5/csv?layers=0 ; listed on data.virginia.gov as prep-report-export-all. 27,134 SEWAGE_RELATED='Y' rows; 2,011 since 2025-01-01 (1,420 typed 'Sanitary Sewer Overflow (SSO)' only).
fields: ORIGINAL_REPORT_* (17 fields incl. REPORTED_DESCRIPTION_OF_INCIDENT, PERMIT_NUMBER, FACILITY_NAME, AGENCIES_NOTIFIED)
cadence: Export refreshed at least daily (rows from 2026-10-30 present on 2026-11-02); same lag as PReP.
license: Hub licenseInfo: 'See DEQ Terms of Use'. Same attribution statement as the PReP page applies.
status_reason: Documented, statistics-capable fallback and backfill for the PReP API; flattened sewage fields; good for history and counts.
notes: TIME TRAP: epoch values equal the local wall-clock time plus 5 hours all year (e.g. API 2026-08-04T19:16:57 = export 1785889017000 = 2026-08-05T00:16:57Z), so in summer they are one hour late if read as UTC. Convert by subtracting 5 h and treating the result as America/New_York wall-clock.

name: DEQ EDMA layer 175 'PReP Reports (Daily)' (points)
access_detail: Point layer (also public/PrepReports/MapServer/1). 33,266 features since 2019-05-29. Query by PRP_REPORT_ID (string): where=PRP_REPORT_ID IN ('324738') &outSR=4326. REFERENCE_POINT 'PG' (geocoded). Fetched four sample points.
fills_event_fields: coordinates (geocoded site address, not the outfall)
license: EDMA service description: 'By viewing and using this data for any purpose, you agree to DEQ's Terms of Use'
status_reason: Only DEQ source of a point per PReP report; join on id to the API record.
notes: Epoch here equals local wall-clock labelled as UTC (different from the export table's +5 h). Points are geocoded site addresses with precision unknown.

name: Va. Code § 62.1-44.5 (prohibition of unpermitted discharges; 24-hour notification)
access_detail: Fetched (raw/vacode-62.1-44.5.html). Subsection B: any person who discharges sewage in violation of subsection A 'shall, upon learning of the discharge, promptly notify, but in no case later than 24 hours the Board, the Director of the Department of Environmental Quality, or the coordinator of emergency services appointed pursuant to § 44-146.19 for the political subdivision reasonably expected to be affected by the discharge. Written notice to the Director of the Department of Environmental Quality shall follow initial notice within the time frame specified by the federal Clean Water Act.' Last amended 2016 (cc. 68, 758).
status_reason: The notice deadline the site can cite: 24 hours, to DEQ or the local emergency coordinator, not to the public.

name: Va. Code § 62.1-44.19:6 (Citizen right-to-know provisions), subsection B
access_detail: Fetched. B: 'The Department of Environmental Quality shall provide to the Virginia Department of Health and local newspapers, television stations, and radio stations, and shall disseminate via official social media accounts and email notification lists, the discharge information reported to the Director of the Department of Environmental Quality pursuant to subsection B of § 62.1-44.5, when the Virginia Department of Health determines that the discharge may be detrimental to the public health or the Department determines that the discharge may impair beneficial uses of state waters.' Added by 2020 cc. 958, 1182 (HB 1205); no deadline is set for DEQ's dissemination. A.2 also requires a 'citizen hot-line'.
status_reason: The only statutory public-notice duty in Virginia; it falls on DEQ, is conditional (VDH or DEQ finding) and has no time limit.
notes: The task brief named §§ 62.1-44.19:3 through :7: § :3 is biosolids land application, :4 definitions, :5 water-quality monitoring and 303(d)/305(b) reporting, :7 impaired-water plans. Only :6 concerns discharge notice.

name: DEQ report HD7 (2021): protocol to decide whether an unpermitted discharge has a de minimis impact
access_detail: WebFetch. Required by 2020 c. 1182. Lists triggers for 'more than de minimis' impact: significant fish kill, VDH shellfish closure, 'Significant non-precipitation-related sewage incident reaching surface waters', HABs, human-contact concern, intake contamination. DEQ preferred the human-based option with existing resources; no gallon threshold; no timeline.
status_reason: Explains why DEQ does not publish every spill: dissemination was scoped to non-de-minimis incidents.

name: 9VAC25-31-190 L and M (VPDES conditions applicable to all permits: reporting, bypass)
access_detail: Fetched. L 6: 'If any unusual or extraordinary discharge including a bypass or upset should occur from a facility and such discharge enters or could be expected to enter state waters, the owner shall promptly notify, in no case later than 24 hours, the department by telephone after the discovery of such discharge... The permittee shall reduce the report to writing and shall submit it to the department within five days of discovery'. L 7 a: noncompliance that may endanger health 'shall be provided orally within 24 hours'; L 7 a (1) lists CSO/SSO/bypass report content (event type, structure type, volumes, impacts, wet weather). L 7 a (2) and L 8 b: electronic submission 'As of the start date in Table 1 of 9VAC25-31-1020'. M 2 a: anticipated bypass notice 'at least 10 days before'.
status_reason: Permit-level deadlines: oral within 24 h, written within 5 days, all to DEQ.

name: 2020 Acts ch. 634 (SB 1064): James River CSO plans and deadlines (Richmond)
access_detail: Fetched. Applies to 'any combined sewer overflow (CSO) system east of Charlottesville that discharges into the James River watershed' (Richmond). Interim plan 2021, final plan by July 1, 2024; 'By July 1, 2035, complete construction and related activities pursuant to the final plan'; annual progress report to DEQ by Dec 1. No public-notification clause.
status_reason: Program context for Richmond; not a notice rule.

name: 2017 Acts chs. 826/827 (HB 2383/SB 898) and 2024 Acts ch. 97 (HB 71): Alexandria CSO compliance deadline
access_detail: Fetched both. 2017 § 3: owners not under an order as of Jan 1, 2017 must 'by July 1, 2025, bring the CSO outfall into compliance'; 2024 ch. 97 changed 2025 to 2026. AlexRenew says RiverRenew went into service July 1, 2026. No public-notification clause.
status_reason: Program context for AlexRenew.

name: 2026 Acts ch. 946 (SB 453): civil penalty for intentional discharge of untreated sewage
access_detail: LIS bill page read in browser: 'Establishes a maximum civil penalty of $50,000 per violation for any person found to have intentionally discharged untreated sewage onto land or into waters of the Commonwealth.' Approved 2026-04-13, effective 2026-07-01. Chaptered text not read; Code section not identified.
status_reason: The only 2023-2026 sewage act found; penalty, not notice. Section histories of §§ 62.1-44.5 (last 2016) and 62.1-44.19:6 (last 2020) confirm no notice amendments since.

name: Va. Code §§ 62.1-44.19:1 and :2 (Virginia Beach and Hampton Roads pump-station requirements)
access_detail: Fetched. :2 requires pump stations in Chesapeake, Hampton, Newport News, Norfolk and Virginia Beach to have alarms, standby pumping and not use overflow lines 'except in an emergency'. No notice duty.
status_reason: Design rule, not notification.

name: Va. Code § 62.1-44.34:19 (reporting of oil discharges)
access_detail: Section listed in the chapter TOC; oil only.
status_reason: Oil, not sewage.

name: Virginia recreational bacteria criteria quoted by DEQ (9VAC25-260-170)
access_detail: As quoted on DEQ's Potomac page: 'Virginia's statistical threshold value for recreational primary contact — 410 counts/100 mL E. coli in freshwater and 130 counts/100 ml Enterococci in transitional and saltwater', and VDH's beach action value '104 /100 ml Enterococci'. Regulation text not fetched.
status_reason: Criteria in the authorities' words; for the science agent.

name: City of Richmond public CSO map (Xylem/EmNet BLU-X 'CSO Map Notification Web Application')
operator: City of Richmond Department of Public Utilities
waters_covered: James River, Gillies Creek, Almond Creek, canals in Richmond (25 monitored outfalls)
access_detail: React app; reads https://restapi.emnet.net/api/tables/{visualizations/47/?uuid=..., analysis-configurations/47/?analysis-type=2, inodes/47/, analysis-results/47/?analysis-configuration-id=257..281&created-on=<UTC now>} with a 'Token' header whose value is embedded in the public bundle (not used directly here). Site list read from the page's own state in the browser pane on 2026-11-02 20:43 EST: 25 sites, all 'monitored', all 'Normal' (no overflow in the last 48 h); 'last' = latest cso_last_occurrence. Saved raw/richmond/emnet/sites-2026-11-02.json.
fills_event_fields: started_at (only the last occurrence per outfall)
cannot_fill: history (only the last event per site)
cadence: Sensor-driven; the app polls on a timer (WRIC 2022: every five minutes). Legend: 'Monitored Site (Overflow*)' ... '*in the last 48 hours'.
history: None in the map; monthly XLSX gives history.
license: No terms on the app. City page: map provided 'as is' (no licence text found).
legal_basis: VPDES permit VA0063177 Part III public notification (signs and website) plus 2020 Acts ch. 634 program
status_reason: Richmond's only near-real-time public CSO channel. Polling it means calling the vendor API with the app's embedded token; the owner must decide whether that is acceptable or ask DPU/Xylem for access.
notes: Richmond page: '* CSO overflow email notifications are no longer provided, as the interactive map provides that data.' CSO 14 is labelled 'CSO 14 Overflow Depth'. Three sites (CSO 18, 19, 33) show no recorded last event.

name: Richmond monthly CSO Outfall Reports (XLSX, per-outfall events)
operator: City of Richmond Department of Public Utilities
access_detail: Links on the CSO Outfalls page: rva.gov/media/{id} redirect pages that embed a sites/default/files/... XLSX (e.g. July 2026: https://rva.gov/sites/default/files/2026-08/47_CSOReports2026_Jul2026_CSO_Report_Public_rtswmm%20%281%29.xlsx). Sheet 'CSO Summary' (sensor type, % good data, activations, observed volume MG) and one sheet per outfall 'CSO_06-Events' with start, end (Excel serials), rainfall in, volume MG, overflow_duration_hours. July 2026: '287.0 MG Overflow Observed'. Parsed to raw/richmond/monthly/jul2026-events.json. Listed months: Jan 2024 - Jul 2026 (Oct 2025 missing).
cadence: Monthly, posted 1-2 months after the month (July 2026 file in a 2026-08 folder; Aug-Oct 2026 not yet posted on 2026-11-02).
status_reason: Authoritative per-outfall history with volumes; pair with the live map.
notes: 'Activations are defined by CSO volumes > 0.01 MG and an interevent time of 72 hours' (sheet note), so 'end' can be days after the duration hours were used.

name: Richmond VPDES Integrated Permit VA0063177 (WWTP, CSS, MS4), effective 2025-09-01
access_detail: Downloaded (90 pages); text extracted with a stream parser. Part III 1.h 'Public Notification. (1) The permittee shall maintain warning signs at all CSOs that are predicted to discharge more frequently than once per summer on average. (2) Publish information on the City's web site pertaining to the CSO Control Program. (3) Attend community meetings to inform citizens of proposed control facilities. (4) Encourage local press coverage of CSO program developments.' Part V: unauthorized discharges reported 'immediately upon discovery of the discharge, but in no case later than 24 hours'. Expiration 2030-08-31.
status_reason: Shows the permit does not require event-by-event public notice; the map is voluntary/plan-driven.

name: HRSD Newsroom news releases (incident releases for major spills)
waters_covered: Hampton Roads, Middle Peninsula, Eastern Shore
access_detail: Fetched. 298 dated items listed for 2025-2026, almost all construction notices and traffic advisories. Spill releases are ad hoc: 2026-08-04 'HRSD Crews Address Pipeline Failure on Douglas Avenue Near Rolfe Terrace in Portsmouth' with updates Aug 5, 6, 7 ('The total spill volume was estimated to be approximately 3.1 million gallons'). notes: HRSD permits: VA0081230 Army Base, VA0081248 Atlantic, VA0081256 Boat Harbor, VA0081264 Chesapeake-Elizabeth, VA0081272 James River, VA0081281 Virginia Initiative, VA0081299 Nansemond, VA0081302 Williamsburg, VA0081311 York River, plus small plants (ECHO). sample_record.title: Recreational Water Advisory Issued for Hull Creek following Sewer Main Break
sample_record.text: The advisory area for Hull Creek extends throughout the Western Branch of the Elizabeth River.

cadence: Same day to 2 days after the spill report (Hull Creek advisory the day after; Bailey Bay 2 days after discovery; Potomac 25 days after the collapse).
license: No licence on releases; public government news.
legal_basis: VDH discretion (no statutory trigger); feeds DEQ's § 62.1-44.19:6 B duty
status_reason: The best official advisory feed: machine-readable RSS with full text and lift notices. Parse titles 'Issued'/'Lifted'.
notes: Wording to quote: 'Out of an abundance of caution'; 'avoid recreational water activities ... where full-body submersion is more likely to occur. Boating activities where full-body submersion is not likely to occur (motor boating, flatwater canoeing or kayaking, and fishing) may continue with proper caution'. VDH lift notes give stop times that can differ from DEQ's (Bailey Bay: VDH 'Tuesday, July 22', DEQ noon Tuesday July 21).
